Earnings Call Transcript
Sensata (ST) Q3 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Oct 28, 2025 at 6:02PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Tuesday, Oct. 28, 2025 at 5 p.m. ET
Call participants
Chief Executive Officer — Stephan von Schuckmann
Chief Financial Officer — Andrew Lynch
Executive Vice President and President, China — Jackie Chan
Incoming Chief Operations Officer — Nicolas Baudoux
Chief Growth and Transformation Officer — Patrick Hertzkin
Vice President, Investor Relations — James Entwistle
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
Risks
Andrew Lynch reported, "In the third quarter, we recorded $259 million in noncash charges as a result of changes in clean energy policy and emissions regulations. This included a goodwill impairment charge of approximately $226 million related to the Dynapower business as well as certain other non-cash charges primarily due to excess capacity related to electrification."
Stephan von Schuckmann said, "Recent changes in clean energy policy and the anticipated slowdown in the clean energy sector made it necessary to reevaluate the book value of this business today."
Takeaways
Revenue
-- $932 million in revenue, down $51 million or 5.2%, mainly due to divestitures and product lifecycle management.
Organic revenue growth
-- Approximately 3% organic year-over-year revenue growth, demonstrating outperformance relative to end markets.
Adjusted operating income
-- $180 million in adjusted operating income, with an adjusted operating margin of 19.3%, up 30 basis points sequentially and 10 basis points year over year.
Adjusted EPS
-- Adjusted earnings per share was $0.89, up $0.02 sequentially and flat year over year despite lower revenue.
Free cash flow
-- $130 million in free cash flow, representing a 49% increase year over year and a 105% conversion rate of adjusted net income.
Net leverage
-- Reduced to 2.9x trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA from 3.0x at June 2025.
Debt reduction
-- The company commenced $350 million in cash tender offers to retire long-term debt.
Return on invested capital
-- Increased to 10.2%, up 10 basis points sequentially and 20 basis points year over year compared to 2024.
Performance Sensing segment
-- Revenue of $657 million, 3.6% organic growth, and adjusted operating margin expansion of 160 basis points year over year to 23.7%.
Sensing Solutions segment
-- Revenue of $275 million, 2.5% organic growth, with margin expansion of 150 basis points year over year to a 30.9% adjusted operating margin.
Dividend
-- Returned $17 million via quarterly dividend; fiscal fourth quarter 2025 dividend of $0.12 per share payable Nov. 26, 2025.
Tire burst detection
-- Business secured with two leading Chinese OEMs; design cycle expected to be six to nine months from win to production in China.
HVAC growth
-- Segment grew to 6% of revenue, up from 4.6% in fiscal second quarter 2025 and over 4% in fiscal third quarter 2024, driven by the HL gas leak detection product and key new customer wins.
2025 fourth quarter guidance
-- Revenue of $890 million to $920 million, adjusted operating income of $172 million to $179 million, adjusted operating margin of 19.3% to 19.5%, and adjusted EPS of $0.83 to $0.87 for the fiscal fourth quarter ending Dec. 31, 2025.
Tariff impact
-- $12 million in tariff costs and related pass-through revenues in 2025, not expected to materially change in the near term.
Summary
Sensata Technologies Holding

(
ST

1.72%
)
reached a milestone in its operational transformation, reporting sequential margin expansion and robust free cash flow conversion above 100% of adjusted net income. New leadership appointments in growth and operations are positioned to drive further strategic execution in key geographies and market segments. The company recast its growth strategy for Dynapower following clean energy policy changes, resulting in a significant noncash goodwill impairment charge of approximately $226 million and a reorientation toward defense, data centers, and grid stabilization applications. Segment-level outgrowth was realized across automotive, HVOR, and Sensing Solutions, with the HL gas leak detection product bolstering HVAC revenue, while early-stage traction was highlighted for tire burst detection in China. Management reiterated a near-term focus on deleveraging and capital discipline, complemented by fiscal fourth quarter guidance reflecting a cautious market outlook and unchanged tariff exposure.
Stephan von Schuckmann said, "Our Q3 results represent a compelling proof point in the progress we have made on operational excellence. The third consecutive quarter we delivered on expectations, reporting results at or above guidance ranges."
Andrew Lynch highlighted persistent capital expenditure discipline as a driver of high free cash flow conversion and reduced leverage.
Product portfolio moves included strategic shifts in Dynapower and market share gains in China automotive, with Jackie Chan promoted to oversee expanded China operations.
Growth headwinds from clean energy have led to valuation adjustments, including a noncash goodwill impairment charge, but industrial, aerospace, and HVAC are noted as primary vectors for near-term expansion.
The company maintains "very comfortable" according to Andrew Lynch defending a 19% adjusted operating margin floor on a full-year basis, and is guiding for low single-digit organic growth if end-market conditions hold.
Industry glossary
HVOR
: Heavy Vehicle and Off-Road, denoting Sensata's segment focused on commercial vehicles and off-highway machinery markets.
Tariff pass-through revenue
: Revenue offsetting incremental tariff costs billed directly to customers as required by trade policy changes.
HL gas leak detection
: Sensata's high-accuracy sensor designed for identifying refrigerant leaks in HVAC and industrial applications, cited as a principal driver of HVAC revenue growth.
Dynapower
: Sensata's business focused on power conversion technologies, including grid stabilization and mission-critical electrification for sectors like defense and data centers.
